text: It's easy enough to hide amongst Cybermen, when you are a Cyberman.
A Cyberman? But I've never... How did they get the ability to do that to you?
Oh, from you. When you gave it to them.
I most certainly did not.
You will. In about 15 minutes time.
Me? But what will I do? How can I stop it?
That's what I'm here to find out.
Their records are very detailed about who you are, but not about what you do and why.
So you're from the future?
Exactly the opposite, actually, but I represent the ultimate development of cybertechnology gone mad.
Flesh made machine.
How much of you is still flesh and blood?
The exterior. Inside, I'm pure Cyberman, but with a brain, not a computer.
Why?
Do you want the story? The whole story?
The Brodie's Notes version would be nice.
In 1927, four days after I was born,
The Cybermen.
The Cybermen brought a virus to Earth.
It attacked the nervous system of all living things, transforming them into a techno-organic hybrid.
Veins and nerves relaced themselves as metallic carriers for cybernetic signals.
The animals died quickly, their brains unable to cope with the shock.
They went catatonic and starved, as did millions of humans.
Whole continents died in days.
The survivors were either converted or fought back and were eradicated.
And you?
As I said, I was a baby.
One of a new generation of skin drones that grew up in a techno-organic world.
Where did the Cybermen develop this virus?
Over the 24 years of my life, I and a limited number of, well, you'd call us rebels, I guess, grew up determined to save our planet and reclaim our humanity.
We stole cybertechnology.
Hundreds sacrificed their lives feeding the rest of us tidbits of knowledge and information purged from the Cybermen's computer database.
We traced a nexus point to 3286.
Here.
This nameless planet where, going by their records, the Cyber Race discovered the ability to manipulate time.
The Cybermen's knowledge of temporal science was without equal.
Oh yes, Doctor.
They crushed your planet and learned all your secrets.
Daleks, Sontarans, Draconians all fell to the new Cyber Race thanks to their ability to time travel.
Crossing from one timeline into a divergent one.
It was nothing now.
And thus you think I'm responsible?
It's a possibility.
So how did you get here?
I left planet Earth, centerpiece of the Cyberverse, in 1951 in a stolen Cybermen Chronosphere.
So you arrived here in our timeline with this.
How did you...
Oh, of course.
You got Isherwood to go through my stuff.
I thought he was behaving oddly earlier.
It's a file of what?
The techno-organic virus?
Sort of.
It's a reversal of theirs.
Huh?
Organic techno, if you like.
We use nanotechnology to imprint upon the virus commands that will decay the metal and plastic implants within a Cyberman.
Render it useless.
Instead of converting our internal organs into technology, once inside the Cybermen, it reverts theirs to a mushy goo.
I doubt they'll survive.
Thank you.
I'll take that.
What, you idiot!
Don't you see what you've done?
What?
You've created a time paradox.
The Cybermen don't have the ability to make a virus like this.
It simply wouldn't occur to them.
It's too illogical.
But if they get your virus, they'll do what you did.
They'll reverse it.
So instead of attacking them, it'll attack flesh again.
They're far more adept at nanotechnology than you probably are.
Is there a point?
They'd have an ultimate weapon.
Once they've got time travel, all they have to do is retrace your steps back to the 20th century and start it again.
Creating the divergent timeline that will become the real timeline, rendering this one, where we are now, the divergent one.
The grandfather paradox.
Or an interesting twist on it.
Interesting twist?
Is that all you care about?
Give the file back to me.
We must destroy it.
Destroy it?
Twenty-four years before I left Earth, you gave them the ability to bring their virus to Earth and start the nightmare that is, or hopefully was, my life.
My entire life.
My entire existence has only been bearable so that I can live for this moment and you want me to throw it away?

The only thing, Doctor, stopping me from killing you now is that without you to protect it, I can't guarantee the Cybermen won't access your TARDIS before I've introduced this little tube of goo to their respiratory systems.
I can't let you do this, Goddard. You must see-
Strength of ten men, Doctor.
With reflexes to match.
Remember that when you wake up.
Goddard just thumped the Doctor.
What are you saying?
Jesus.
Boss lady, are you all right?
Richard, look out!
Why is the Doctor lying down?
The head could crush it. Stop it, please.
For God's sake, you're hurting him.
Answer me.
Goddard thumped him.
Goddard knocked the Doctor down.
Please, Dad.
I don't know why.
Ask him. He's coming back.
Who is?
Goddard.
What is a Goddard?
You, Dad. You came with him on the mothership.
You must remember.
Please.
Probe. Probe Nicholas Savage's memories.
Non-relevant information has been purged.
You're breaking my head.
What is Goddard?
Hello, Nicky. I am.
I repeat, what or who is Goddard?
He's right beside you. Him.
You are incorrect.
Fascinating.
For crying out loud, Goddard, tell us what you think the like.
Tell me.
He's there.
Goddard.
Run!
God!
God!
He's coming!
Oh Goddard.
Strength of 10 men.
For God's sake, Goddard.
You will come with me.
The Controller requires your presence.
Why me?
And please don't hurt me.
I'll tell you what you want to know.
Please.
Goddard.
Help!
Sorry, Wrenchard.
Doctor.
I thought you were expendable.
All is fair in love and one.
warrant on that. So that's what a hedgehog hit by an articulated truck feels like. Oh, Goddard.
Goddard! Wakey, wakey, doctor. We ought to see about following them. Why did it take the
administrator? Where's Mr. Renshard? Renshard got a head start on the carnage that's about to be
unleashed here. Unleashed by you and your virus, no doubt. That's the plan. I need to get Evelyn
out of the controller's grip. If he's been monitoring things, he'll know what's going on now.
Then I'll deal with you. Forgive me for saying this, doctor, but you are expendable. So is
Evelyn, Isherwood, the mothership, everything. The only thing that matters is my mission.
I misjudged you, Goddard. I thought that despite your ridiculous plan, you had some morals,
some scruples, some shred of humanity left within you. Your morality, doctor, is a luxury my people
have learned to live without. Your fault, remember? How can it be my fault? I haven't
done anything. Yet. We have minutes before the temporal wave hits. Why have the reports from
the planet ceased? The sniper commander is within the structure, bringing administrator Isherwood.
The temporal wave is due in moments. Where is the doctor? What will happen if he's hit by your
temporal wave? Well, surely he'll just be swept in here. Only humans within the structure,
have been dragged back through the portal. Those on the surface were aged to death in
microseconds. And for a time, Lord, that may take four or five seconds. Seconds of pain,
excruciating pain. My controller, you sounded almost human then. So where are the others?
Others? Osborn, the other two teams. There is not enough energy here to maintain them or to extend
them.
The range of the portal. They have been converted and are now in hibernation,
awaiting my signal to revive. Trooper, controller, this human is of no further use.
Take it to the conversion chamber and prepare to extract its brain. The body can be disposed of.
It is too frail to accept cyber technology. I'm tougher than I look, controller. You should keep
me around. You might...
You might need the odd arm or leg. Don't worry about the hip, I can feel a touch of
rheumatism in that. But the rest of me is good for a few years yet.
Take her away, now!
You're losing your cool, controller. I've seen department heads get like that when they
realised they'd buggered up their annual accounts. They didn't frighten me, either.
Convert her, now!
What are you so scared of, controller?
Now!
Look, Goddard. The portal is open.
Portal's activated. And fading.
I guess Savage took Isherwood through.
You are the doctor. You are required.
I forgot about the fact that Savage had two guards.
Goddard, a little assistance from the Invisible Man?
You will.
Well, a bit of a hurried field test, but the virus works.
Too well. You killed it.
Wait. Let's have a look under the faceplate.
Of course. Osborn's military commander.
So what?
Nothing. Just habit.
When we killed Cybermen back home, we'd always check the face, just to see who we'd helped.
Helped?
We released them from their pain.
We honor them by knowing their faces and names, if possible.
As you suggested, our moralities are many miles apart.
Shall we go through?
Doctor?
What now?
Half the virus just... vaporized.
Damn it. Something in that portal counters it.
There's not much left.
Shame it didn't all go.
I wonder why.
Controller, the last Cyberman in the structure has ceased functioning.
The doctor.
What of this one?
Please, don't hurt me. I can help you.
You need to know things about 3286, yes?
I can tell you. We could come to a deal.
You are of no use to me.
I could take you through to my time.
I cannot go through.
Through the portal.
What? Why?
Observe. Commander, escort him to the portal.
Now what are you doing?
Examining these hieroglyphs on this side, comparing my earlier notes.
Yes! Yes, I see.
Can we get a move on?
Wait a minute. It's the instruction manual we talked about earlier.
Yes, so if I do this, and this...
Do what?
A bit of sabotage.
What exactly?
There. And I hope that works.
And I hope we've enough time.
What have you done?
I'm not telling you. It might appeal to your morality.
And it certainly offends mine.
Human, observe the membrane within the portal.
Okay.
Control Up. This action is not recommended.
It is merely my hand. It will revert once I return it through the membrane.
Observe, Human.
My god, your hand! It's becoming human.
Observe.
It is aging. Decaying.
The portal affects me in a different way from others.
Now my hand is back in this time zone. It has healed. The suit regenerated.
Fascinating. But why were you affected differently?
That information is not known.
So why are Savage and the others half-human still?
When I first arrived here.
I was dying.
My last three troopers went through the membrane.
And were destroyed when the temporal wave was triggered.
And with them gone.
You had only a limited amount of technology.
As each human was washed back through here.
It was only possible to utilize the minimum requirement to convert them.
Why are you telling me this? If you say I can't help you?
I rather think he's telling me.
Doctor! Goddard!
Again, Goddard. What is Goddard?
Cary, you don't want to do this, do you? Please, stop.
Remember who you are.
I must convert you.
Cary, this will kill me. Make me like you.
You will be like us.
No!
You will be like us.
No!
No!
No!
